001package io.jstach.rainbowgum;
002
003import java.io.UncheckedIOException;
004import java.net.URI;
005import java.nio.ByteBuffer;
006import java.nio.CharBuffer;
007import java.nio.charset.CharacterCodingException;
008import java.nio.charset.Charset;
009import java.nio.charset.CharsetEncoder;
010import java.nio.charset.CodingErrorAction;
011import java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets;
012import java.util.Objects;
013
014import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;
015
016import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogOutput.ContentType;
017import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogOutput.ContentType.StandardContentType;
018import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogOutput.WriteMethod;
019import io.jstach.rainbowgum.format.AbstractStandardEventFormatter;
020import io.jstach.rainbowgum.format.StandardEventFormatter;
021
022/**
023 * Encodes a {@link LogEvent} into a buffer of its choosing. While the {@link Buffer} does
024 * not need to be thread-safe the encoder itself should be.
025 * <p>
026 * An appender typically calls an encoder by first {@linkplain #buffer(BufferHints)
027 * creating a buffer} that the encoder knows about or reusing an existing {@link Buffer}
028 * the encoder knows about.
029 * <p>
030 * The {@linkplain #encode(LogEvent, Buffer) encoding into a buffer} typically happens
031 * outside of lock to minimize lock contention. Thus the appender promises not to share a
032 * buffer at the same time with other threads as well as only use a buffer the log encoder
033 * created at some point.
034 * <p>
035 * Once encoding is done the appender than typically enters into a lock (appenders
036 * attached to an async publisher may not need to use a lock) where the appender will ask
037 * the buffer to {@linkplain Buffer#drain(LogOutput, LogEvent) drain} its contents into
038 * the output.
039 * <p>
040 * Because {@link Buffer} is not a specific implementation the Encoder typically casts the
041 * buffer to the expected concrete implementation. {@link AbstractEncoder} can make this
042 * logic easier and is recommended to extend it.
043 * <p>
044 * Given the complexity of encoders it is recommend use the much easier to implement
045 * interface of {@link LogFormatter} and convert it to an encoder with
046 * {@link #of(LogFormatter)}.
047 *
048 * @see LogFormatter
049 * @see Buffer
050 * @see LogAppender
051 */
052public interface LogEncoder {
053
054        /**
055         * Creates a <strong>new</strong> buffer. The encoder should not try to reuse buffers
056         * as that is the responsibility of the {@linkplain LogAppender appender} (and
057         * possibly {@link LogOutput} but usually not). Hints can be retrieved by call
058         * {@link LogOutput#bufferHints()}.
059         * @param hints hints are like size and storage type etc.
060         * @return a new buffer.
061         * @apiNote hints can be retrieved by calling {@link LogOutput#bufferHints()} the
062         * reason the output itself is not passed is to prevent the buffer from using the
063         * output directly at an inappropriate time as well as the rare possibility of the
064         * buffer being used by multiple outputs.
065         */
066        public Buffer buffer(BufferHints hints);
067
068        /**
069         * Encodes an event to the buffer. It is recommended that the encoder call
070         * {@link Buffer#clear()} before using.
071         * @param event log event.
072         * @param buffer buffer created from {@link #buffer(BufferHints)}.
073         */
074        public void encode(LogEvent event, Buffer buffer);
075
076        /**
077         * Creates an encoder from a formatter that encodes with
078         * {@link StandardCharsets#UTF_8}. For anything more than the default charset/content
079         * type/max buffer size use {@link #builder(LogFormatter)}.
080         * @param formatter formatter.
081         * @return encoder.
082         */
083        public static LogProvider<LogEncoder> of(LogFormatter formatter) {
084                return builder(formatter).build();
085        }
086
087        /**
088         * Creates a builder for an encoder backed by the given formatter.
089         * @param formatter formatter.
090         * @return builder.
091         */
092        public static Builder builder(LogFormatter formatter) {
093                return new Builder(formatter);
094        }
095
096        /**
097         * Creates a builder for an encoder backed by the default TTLL
098         * ({@link io.jstach.rainbowgum.format.StandardEventFormatter}) formatter.
099         * @return builder.
100         */
101        public static Builder builder() {
102                return new Builder(StandardEventFormatter.builder().build());
103        }
104
105        /**
106         * Builds a {@link LogEncoder} out of a {@link LogFormatter}.
107         *
108         * @apiNote created with {@link LogEncoder#builder(LogFormatter)} or
109         * {@link LogEncoder#builder()}.
110         */
111        public static final class Builder {
112
113                private final LogFormatter formatter;
114
115                private @Nullable Charset charset;
116
117                private @Nullable ContentType contentType;
118
119                private int maxBufferSize = -1;
120
121                private int initialBufferSize = DirectByteBufferBuffer.DEFAULT_INITIAL_BYTE_CAPACITY;
122
123                private Builder(LogFormatter formatter) {
124                        this.formatter = Objects.requireNonNull(formatter);
125                }
126
127                /**
128                 * Charset to encode with. Only affects outputs whose
129                 * {@link BufferHints#writeMethod()} is {@link WriteMethod#BYTES} or
130                 * {@link WriteMethod#BYTE_BUFFER} - the {@link WriteMethod#STRING} path hands a
131                 * plain {@link String} to {@link LogOutput#write(LogEvent, String)}, whose own
132                 * default implementation is fixed to {@link StandardCharsets#UTF_8} regardless of
133                 * this setting, but no built-in output actually uses that write method. Defaults
134                 * to {@link StandardCharsets#UTF_8}, or to {@link #contentType(ContentType)}'s
135                 * own charset if that was set and this was not. If both are set this charset is
136                 * what is actually used to encode; {@link #contentType(ContentType)} still
137                 * controls what is reported to the output.
138                 * @param charset charset to encode with.
139                 * @return this.
140                 */
141                public Builder charset(Charset charset) {
142                        this.charset = Objects.requireNonNull(charset);
143                        return this;
144                }
145
146                /**
147                 * Content type reported to the output. Use this when the formatter produces
148                 * something other than plain text. Defaults to
149                 * {@link StandardContentType#TEXT_PLAIN} with whatever charset is in effect (see
150                 * {@link #charset(Charset)}).
151                 * @param contentType content type reported to the output.
152                 * @return this.
153                 */
154                public Builder contentType(ContentType contentType) {
155                        this.contentType = Objects.requireNonNull(contentType);
156                        return this;
157                }
158
159                /**
160                 * Configures a maximum buffer size - see {@link Buffer#isOversized()}. This is a
161                 * <strong>soft ceiling, not a hard cap</strong>: a single event can still grow
162                 * the buffer past this size while it is being encoded (nothing here truncates or
163                 * rejects an oversized event), it just means the buffer's backing storage gets
164                 * shrunk back down afterward instead of being kept at its grown size indefinitely
165                 * - a quota that gets reclaimed after the fact, not enforced during the write.
166                 * This, like charset, is a property of the encoder/buffer itself, not of whatever
167                 * ends up reusing the buffer (e.g. an appender's {@code ThreadLocal}-cached one)
168                 * - the buffer decides for itself, inside its own {@link Buffer#clear()}, whether
169                 * to shrink.
170                 * @param maxBufferSize a negative value disables {@link Buffer#isOversized()}
171                 * entirely (the default).
172                 * @return this.
173                 */
174                public Builder maxBufferSize(int maxBufferSize) {
175                        this.maxBufferSize = maxBufferSize;
176                        return this;
177                }
178
179                /**
180                 * The capacity a fresh buffer is allocated with before any event has been encoded
181                 * into it. Defaults to
182                 * {@link DirectByteBufferBuffer#DEFAULT_INITIAL_BYTE_CAPACITY}.
183                 * @param initialBufferSize initial buffer capacity, must be positive.
184                 * @return this.
185                 * @throws IllegalArgumentException if not positive.
186                 */
187                public Builder initialBufferSize(int initialBufferSize) {
188                        if (initialBufferSize <= 0) {
189                                throw new IllegalArgumentException("initialBufferSize must be positive: " + initialBufferSize);
190                        }
191                        this.initialBufferSize = initialBufferSize;
192                        return this;
193                }
194
195                /**
196                 * Builds the encoder.
197                 * @return encoder.
198                 */
199                public LogProvider<LogEncoder> build() {
200                        Charset c = charset;
201                        ContentType ct = contentType;
202                        if (ct != null) {
203                                if (c == null) {
204                                        c = ct.charsetOrNull();
205                                }
206                        }
207                        if (c == null) {
208                                c = StandardCharsets.UTF_8;
209                        }
210                        if (ct == null) {
211                                ct = ContentType.of(StandardContentType.TEXT_PLAIN.contentType(), c);
212                        }
213                        var resolvedCharset = c;
214                        var resolvedContentType = ct;
215                        return (n, config) -> new FormatterEncoder(formatter, resolvedCharset, resolvedContentType, maxBufferSize,
216                                        initialBufferSize, config.metrics());
217                }
218
219        }
220
221        /**
222         * Provides a lazy loaded encoder from a URI.
223         * @param uri uri.
224         * @return provider of encoder.
225         */
226        public static LogProvider<LogEncoder> of(URI uri) {
227                return of(LogProviderRef.of(uri));
228        }
229
230        /**
231         * Provides the standard TTLL encoder.
232         * @return provider of encoder.
233         */
234        public static LogProvider<LogEncoder> ofTTLL() {
235                return of(LogProviderRef.of(URI.create(AbstractStandardEventFormatter.SCHEMA)));
236        }
237
238        /**
239         * Provides a lazy loaded encoder from a provider ref.
240         * @param ref uri.
241         * @return provider of output.
242         * @apiNote the provider may throw an {@link UncheckedIOException}.
243         */
244        public static LogProvider<LogEncoder> of(LogProviderRef ref) {
245                return (s, c) -> {
246                        return c.encoderRegistry().provide(ref).provide(s, c);
247                };
248        }
249
250        /**
251         * Finds output based on URI.
252         */
253        public interface EncoderProvider {
254
255                /**
256                 * Loads an encoder from a URI.
257                 * @param ref reference to provider usually just a uri.
258                 * @return output.
259                 * @throws LogProviderRef.NotFoundException if there is no registered provider.
260                 */
261                LogProvider<LogEncoder> provide(LogProviderRef ref) throws LogProviderRef.NotFoundException;
262
263                /**
264                 * Convenience method to register encoders that require no configuration.
265                 * @param encoder already configured encoder.
266                 * @return encoder provider.
267                 */
268                static EncoderProvider of(LogProvider<LogEncoder> encoder) {
269                        return ref -> encoder;
270                }
271
272        }
273
274        /**
275         * Encoders buffer.
276         */
277        public interface Buffer extends AutoCloseable {
278
279                /**
280                 * The appender will call this usually within a lock to transfer content from the
281                 * buffer to the output.
282                 * @param output output to receive content.
283                 * @param event log event.
284                 */
285                public void drain(LogOutput output, LogEvent event);
286
287                /**
288                 * Prepare the buffer for reuse.
289                 * <p>
290                 * An appender may not call clear before being passed to the encoder so the
291                 * encoder should do its own clearing.
292                 * <p>
293                 * Built-in implementations also shrink their own backing storage back down here
294                 * if {@link #isOversized()} - see that method - so a single unusually large event
295                 * does not permanently bloat a buffer that gets reused for many more events after
296                 * it.
297                 */
298                public void clear();
299
300                /**
301                 * Whether this buffer has grown large enough (its capacity, not how much of that
302                 * capacity the last event actually used) that its backing storage is worth
303                 * shrinking back down rather than kept at its grown size indefinitely - reused
304                 * buffers only grow on their own, they never shrink back down without deliberate
305                 * help. This is a soft ceiling checked between events, not a hard cap enforced
306                 * during one: nothing here stops a single event from growing the buffer past
307                 * whatever threshold it was configured with while that event is being encoded.
308                 * Built-in implementations consult this themselves inside {@link #clear()} to
309                 * decide whether to shrink their own backing storage in place (e.g.
310                 * {@link StringBuilder#trimToSize()}, or reallocating a smaller
311                 * {@link java.nio.ByteBuffer}) - most callers do not need to call this directly;
312                 * it remains here mainly for tests/observability and for a custom {@link Buffer}
313                 * implementation that wants the same self-shrinking behavior.
314                 * <p>
315                 * What "large enough" means, and whether it means anything at all, is entirely up
316                 * to the buffer/encoder - the same way charset is an encoder concern rather than
317                 * something an appender configures (see
318                 * {@link LogEncoder#builder(LogFormatter)}). The default implementation returns
319                 * {@code false} - a buffer implementation that does not override this, or an
320                 * encoder that never configured a threshold, never shrinks.
321                 * @return {@code true} if this buffer's backing storage has grown past whatever
322                 * threshold it was configured with.
323                 */
324                default boolean isOversized() {
325                        return false;
326                }
327
328                /**
329                 * Convenience that will call clear.
330                 */
331                @Override
332                default void close() {
333                        clear();
334                }
335
336        }
337
338        /**
339         * Hints the output can pass to the encoder for creating buffers like max size and
340         * storage style of the buffer etc.
341         *
342         * @apiNote There is no guarantees the encoder/buffer will honor these hints.
343         */
344        public interface BufferHints {
345
346                /*
347                 * TODO should we seal this?
348                 */
349
350                /**
351                 * The preferred write style of the output.
352                 * @return write method.
353                 * @apiNote {@link WriteMethod} implements this interface for convenience.
354                 */
355                LogOutput.WriteMethod writeMethod();
356
357                /**
358                 * Maximum size of the buffer. This is a way for the encoder to say it can only
359                 * handle so much data per event.
360                 * @return a negative number indicates size is not important.
361                 */
362                default int maximumSize() {
363                        return -1;
364                }
365
366        }
367
368        /**
369         * Abstract encoder that will cast the buffer to the desired implementation. Extend to
370         * make creating encoders easier.
371         *
372         * @param <T> buffer type.
373         */
374        abstract class AbstractEncoder<T extends Buffer> implements LogEncoder {
375
376                /**
377                 * Do nothing constructor.
378                 */
379                protected AbstractEncoder() {
380
381                }
382
383                /**
384                 * Create a specific buffer implementation.
385                 * @param hints buffer creation hints.
386                 * @return buffer
387                 */
388                protected abstract T doBuffer(BufferHints hints);
389
390                /**
391                 * A type safe version of {@link #encode(LogEvent, Buffer)}.
392                 * @param event event.
393                 * @param buffer casted buffer.
394                 */
395                protected abstract void doEncode(LogEvent event, T buffer);
396
397                @Override
398                public final Buffer buffer(BufferHints hints) {
399                        return doBuffer(hints);
400                }
401
402                @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
403                @Override
404                public final void encode(LogEvent event, Buffer buffer) {
405                        doEncode(event, (T) buffer);
406
407                }
408
409        }
410
411}
412
413/**
414 * A {@link LogEncoder.Buffer} that formats a {@link LogEvent} through a
415 * {@link LogFormatter} into some intermediate text representation before
416 * {@linkplain #drain(LogOutput, LogEvent) draining} it to the output - the common shape
417 * shared by {@link StringBuilderBuffer} and {@link DirectByteBufferBuffer}, letting
418 * {@link FormatterEncoder} dispatch to either without needing to know which concrete
419 * implementation it has.
420 */
421sealed interface TextBuffer extends LogEncoder.Buffer {
422
423        /**
424         * Formats {@code event} with {@code formatter} into this buffer's own backing
425         * storage, ready to be {@linkplain #drain(LogOutput, LogEvent) drained}. Does not
426         * call {@link #clear()} first - the caller is expected to do that.
427         * @param formatter formatter to format with.
428         * @param event event to format.
429         */
430        public void encodeToBuffer(LogFormatter formatter, LogEvent event);
431
432}
433
434/**
435 * A buffer that simply wraps a {@link StringBuilder}. Direct access to the
436 * {@link StringBuilder} is available as the field {@link #stringBuilder}.
437 *
438 * @see AbstractEncoder
439 */
440final class StringBuilderBuffer implements TextBuffer {
441
442        /**
443         * Underlying StringBuilder.
444         */
445        public final StringBuilder stringBuilder;
446
447        private final int maxBufferSize;
448
449        private final LogMetrics metrics;
450
451        /**
452         * Creates a StringBuilder based buffer that reports {@link #isOversized()} once
453         * {@code sb}'s capacity exceeds {@code maxBufferSize}, reporting
454         * {@link LogMetrics#BUFFER_TRIMMED_METRIC} to {@code metrics} each time
455         * {@link #clear()} actually shrinks the backing storage.
456         * @param sb string builder.
457         * @param maxBufferSize a negative value disables {@link #isOversized()} entirely
458         * (always {@code false}).
459         * @param metrics where to report {@link LogMetrics#BUFFER_TRIMMED_METRIC}.
460         * @return buffer.
461         */
462        public static StringBuilderBuffer of(StringBuilder sb, int maxBufferSize, LogMetrics metrics) {
463                return new StringBuilderBuffer(sb, maxBufferSize, metrics);
464        }
465
466        private StringBuilderBuffer(StringBuilder stringBuilder, int maxBufferSize, LogMetrics metrics) {
467                super();
468                this.stringBuilder = stringBuilder;
469                this.maxBufferSize = maxBufferSize;
470                this.metrics = metrics;
471        }
472
473        @Override
474        public void drain(LogOutput output, LogEvent event) {
475                output.write(event, stringBuilder.toString());
476        }
477
478        @Override
479        public void clear() {
480                stringBuilder.setLength(0);
481                // setLength(0) never touches capacity, so isOversized() here still
482                // reflects growth from whatever was just written - trimToSize()
483                // mutates the StringBuilder in place, no reassignment needed (works
484                // fine through the public final field above).
485                if (isOversized()) {
486                        stringBuilder.trimToSize();
487                        metrics.warnCounter(LogMetrics.BUFFER_TRIMMED_METRIC, 1);
488                }
489        }
490
491        @Override
492        public boolean isOversized() {
493                return maxBufferSize >= 0 && stringBuilder.capacity() > maxBufferSize;
494        }
495
496        @Override
497        public void encodeToBuffer(LogFormatter formatter, LogEvent event) {
498                formatter.format(stringBuilder, event);
499        }
500
501}
502
503/**
504 * A buffer that formats into a reused {@link StringBuilder} (like
505 * {@link StringBuilderBuffer}) but encodes directly into a reused {@link ByteBuffer} via
506 * a {@link CharsetEncoder}, instead of going through an intermediate {@code String} and
507 * {@code byte[]} the way {@code LogOutput.write(LogEvent, String)}'s default
508 * implementation does. This is the same technique
509 * <a href="https://logging.apache.org/log4j/2.x/manual/garbagefree.html">Log4j2's
510 * garbage-free logging</a> uses.
511 * <p>
512 * The {@link CharsetEncoder} work happens in {@link #encodeToByteBuffer()}, called by
513 * {@link #encodeToBuffer(LogFormatter, LogEvent)} - i.e. before
514 * {@link #drain(LogOutput, LogEvent) drain}, which appenders that separate formatting
515 * from writing ({@code LockThreadLocalBufferLogAppender},
516 * {@code SynchronizedThreadLocalBufferLogAppender}) call outside their lock.
517 * {@code drain} - called from inside the lock - therefore does nothing but write the
518 * already-encoded bytes, matching how Log4j2 confines the actual character-to-byte
519 * transcoding to a thread-local scratch buffer and synchronizes only the final copy into
520 * the shared destination.
521 * <p>
522 * Constructed for a specific {@link LogOutput.WriteMethod} - either
523 * {@link LogOutput.WriteMethod#BYTE_BUFFER}, in which case {@link #drain} calls
524 * {@link LogOutput#write(LogEvent, ByteBuffer, LogOutput.ContentType)} directly, or
525 * {@link LogOutput.WriteMethod#BYTES}, in which case {@link #drain} calls
526 * {@link LogOutput#write(LogEvent, byte[], int, int, LogOutput.ContentType)} using the
527 * backing array directly, rather than going through
528 * {@code LogOutput#write(LogEvent, ByteBuffer, ContentType)}'s default implementation
529 * (which would allocate a fresh {@code byte[]} copy every call for an output that does
530 * not itself implement that overload).
531 * <p>
532 * Not thread-safe. Like all {@link LogEncoder.Buffer}s it relies on the appender to
533 * guarantee no overlapping use.
534 */
535final class DirectByteBufferBuffer implements TextBuffer {
536
537        /**
538         * Default initial byte buffer capacity, matching Log4j2's own
539         * {@code log4j2.encoderByteBufferSize} default.
540         */
541        public static final int DEFAULT_INITIAL_BYTE_CAPACITY = 8192;
542
543        /**
544         * The buffer the formatter writes characters into.
545         */
546        public final StringBuilder stringBuilder = new StringBuilder();
547
548        private final CharsetEncoder charsetEncoder;
549
550        private final LogOutput.WriteMethod writeMethod;
551
552        private final LogOutput.ContentType contentType;
553
554        private final int maxBufferSize;
555
556        private final int initialByteCapacity;
557
558        private final LogMetrics metrics;
559
560        private ByteBuffer byteBuffer;
561
562        /**
563         * Creates a buffer with the given write method, initial byte capacity, charset,
564         * content type to report to the output, and maximum combined size (see
565         * {@link #isOversized()}).
566         * @param writeMethod which {@link LogOutput#write} overload {@link #drain} should
567         * call - {@link LogOutput.WriteMethod#BYTES} or
568         * {@link LogOutput.WriteMethod#BYTE_BUFFER}.
569         * @param initialByteCapacity initial capacity of the byte buffer. It will grow
570         * (doubling, or to whatever a single event needs if larger) as needed and the grown
571         * capacity is kept for subsequent events.
572         * @param charset charset to encode with.
573         * @param contentType content type reported to {@link LogOutput#write}. Its
574         * {@link LogOutput.ContentType#charsetOrNull() charset}, if specified, should
575         * normally match {@code charset}.
576         * @param maxBufferSize a negative value disables {@link #isOversized()} entirely
577         * (always {@code false}). Since {@code initialByteCapacity} (commonly
578         * {@value #DEFAULT_INITIAL_BYTE_CAPACITY}) is allocated up front and counted by
579         * {@link #isOversized()} regardless of how much of it any event has actually used, a
580         * {@code maxBufferSize} at or below {@code initialByteCapacity} makes
581         * {@link #isOversized()} unconditionally {@code true} from the very first event -
582         * {@code maxBufferSize} should normally be set well above whatever initial capacity
583         * is in play.
584         * @param metrics where to report {@link LogMetrics#BUFFER_TRIMMED_METRIC} each time
585         * {@link #clear()} actually shrinks the backing storage.
586         */
587        DirectByteBufferBuffer(LogOutput.WriteMethod writeMethod, int initialByteCapacity, Charset charset,
588                        LogOutput.ContentType contentType, int maxBufferSize, LogMetrics metrics) {
589                this.writeMethod = writeMethod;
590                this.byteBuffer = ByteBuffer.allocate(initialByteCapacity);
591                this.charsetEncoder = charset.newEncoder()
592                        .onMalformedInput(CodingErrorAction.REPLACE)
593                        .onUnmappableCharacter(CodingErrorAction.REPLACE);
594                this.contentType = contentType;
595                this.maxBufferSize = maxBufferSize;
596                this.initialByteCapacity = initialByteCapacity;
597                this.metrics = metrics;
598        }
599
600        /**
601         * Writes the already-encoded bytes to the output. Assumes
602         * {@link #encodeToBuffer(LogFormatter, LogEvent)} has already been called for this
603         * event - see the class doc for why that step happens there instead of here.
604         */
605        @Override
606        public void drain(LogOutput output, LogEvent event) {
607                switch (writeMethod) {
608                        case BYTE_BUFFER -> output.write(event, byteBuffer, contentType);
609                        case BYTES -> output.write(event, byteBuffer.array(), byteBuffer.arrayOffset() + byteBuffer.position(),
610                                        byteBuffer.remaining(), contentType);
611                        case STRING ->
612                                throw new IllegalStateException("DirectByteBufferBuffer does not support WriteMethod.STRING");
613                }
614        }
615
616        @Override
617        public void encodeToBuffer(LogFormatter formatter, LogEvent event) {
618                formatter.format(stringBuilder, event);
619                encodeToByteBuffer();
620        }
621
622        /**
623         * Encodes the current contents of {@link #stringBuilder} into the reused
624         * {@link ByteBuffer}, growing it first if needed. Deliberately not called from
625         * {@link #drain(LogOutput, LogEvent)} - see the class doc.
626         */
627        private void encodeToByteBuffer() {
628                int maxBytes = (int) Math.ceil(stringBuilder.length() * (double) charsetEncoder.maxBytesPerChar());
629                if (byteBuffer.capacity() < maxBytes) {
630                        byteBuffer = ByteBuffer.allocate(Math.max(maxBytes, byteBuffer.capacity() * 2));
631                }
632                byteBuffer.clear();
633                charsetEncoder.reset();
634                CharBuffer cb = CharBuffer.wrap(stringBuilder);
635                var result = charsetEncoder.encode(cb, byteBuffer, true);
636                if (result.isError()) {
637                        try {
638                                result.throwException();
639                        }
640                        catch (CharacterCodingException e) {
641                                throw new UncheckedIOException(e);
642                        }
643                }
644                /*
645                 * maxBytes above already sized the buffer to fit the worst case so flush should
646                 * never overflow, but check defensively rather than silently truncate.
647                 */
648                var flushResult = charsetEncoder.flush(byteBuffer);
649                if (flushResult.isOverflow()) {
650                        throw new IllegalStateException("CharsetEncoder flush overflowed despite pre-sized buffer");
651                }
652                byteBuffer.flip();
653        }
654
655        @Override
656        public void clear() {
657                stringBuilder.setLength(0);
658                // Checked before byteBuffer is touched below, so this still reflects
659                // growth from whatever was just drained. stringBuilder.trimToSize()
660                // mutates in place; byteBuffer isn't final (it's already reassigned
661                // during growth in encodeToByteBuffer()) so reallocating it back down
662                // here needs no new field-mutability changes either.
663                if (isOversized()) {
664                        stringBuilder.trimToSize();
665                        byteBuffer = ByteBuffer.allocate(initialByteCapacity);
666                        metrics.warnCounter(LogMetrics.BUFFER_TRIMMED_METRIC, 1);
667                }
668        }
669
670        @Override
671        public boolean isOversized() {
672                return maxBufferSize >= 0 && (stringBuilder.capacity() + byteBuffer.capacity()) > maxBufferSize;
673        }
674
675}
676
677/*
678 * Not an AbstractEncoder since it needs to hand out either a StringBuilderBuffer or a
679 * DirectByteBufferBuffer depending on the output's WriteMethod hint - see buffer(hints).
680 */
681final class FormatterEncoder implements LogEncoder {
682
683        private final LogFormatter formatter;
684
685        private final Charset charset;
686
687        private final ContentType contentType;
688
689        private final int maxBufferSize;
690
691        private final int initialBufferSize;
692
693        private final LogMetrics metrics;
694
695        FormatterEncoder(LogFormatter formatter, Charset charset, ContentType contentType, int maxBufferSize,
696                        int initialBufferSize, LogMetrics metrics) {
697                super();
698                this.formatter = formatter;
699                this.charset = charset;
700                this.contentType = contentType;
701                this.maxBufferSize = maxBufferSize;
702                this.initialBufferSize = initialBufferSize;
703                this.metrics = metrics;
704        }
705
706        @Override
707        public Buffer buffer(BufferHints hints) {
708                return switch (hints.writeMethod()) {
709                        case STRING -> StringBuilderBuffer.of(new StringBuilder(initialBufferSize), maxBufferSize, metrics);
710                        case BYTES, BYTE_BUFFER -> new DirectByteBufferBuffer(hints.writeMethod(), initialBufferSize, charset,
711                                        contentType, maxBufferSize, metrics);
712                };
713        }
714
715        @Override
716        public void encode(LogEvent event, Buffer buffer) {
717                switch (buffer) {
718                        case TextBuffer tb -> {
719                                tb.clear();
720                                tb.encodeToBuffer(formatter, event);
721                        }
722                        default -> throw new IllegalStateException("Unsupported buffer: " + buffer.getClass());
723                }
724        }
725
726}
